sample_unit: LLMs evaluated on four medical QA benchmarks

links.outcome: Chain-of-thought response to clinically motivated input and chain perturbations
links.effect: Chain-Decoupling Rate 72.9% panel-wide on clinically meaningful destructive edits; chain corruption leaves accuracy unchanged; removing CoT prompting does not reduce accuracy.
links.quote: the Chain-Decoupling Rate (CDR; chain does not register the edit and the answer does not flip) is 72.9% panel-wide on clinically meaningful destructive edits, chain corruption leaves accuracy unchanged, and removing CoT prompting does not reduce accuracy.

unlisted_practices: Perturbation audit of chain-of-thought faithfulness using the Chain-Decoupling Rate

screen.reason: Evaluates medical chain-of-thought faithfulness and failure modes across 14 LLMs using a clinical perturbation audit benchmark with clinician-annotated question variants.
